newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open little changed.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open mostly unchanged Monday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, dealers said.
Friday, July ended 0.12 cent lower at 73.04 cents a lb after trading from 73.45 to 72.50 cents. New-crop December finished up 0.07 cent at 75.23 cents.

Despite the weaker close, traders said the market probably found a near-term bottom. They expect July to begin to move higher and toward resistance pegged at 73.50 cents followed by 74.10 cents, where buy stops are expected to be resting.
Fundamentally, Pakistan said today its 1996/97 crop reached a provisional 8.744 million 375-lb bales, down from 9.947 million bales in the same year-ago period.

Planting conditions improved in the U.S. Delta and Southeast, where rain and cold temperatures have kept the crop out of the ground. Still, progress remains behind schedule, Weather Services Corp, said.
Planting is also improving in the Texas High Plains as temperatures rise and soil temperatures imporve.
